Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English. As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

candidates.cover_letter:
TY MATTHEWS, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)
Rock Hill, SC • (704) 999-3605 • Matthewstydsw27@gmail.com

October 27, 2026
Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, NC

Re: Clinic Director: Adolescent Mental Health | Launch AWA North Carolina

Dear Hiring Committee:
I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

Dear Hiring and Clinical Education Team,
I am writing to express my interest in exploring a Master of Social Work (MSW) practicum placement with your organizations in Davie, Florida, specifically Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Through my work as a Direct Services Coordinator with Housing Matters, I provided trauma-informed support to individuals experiencing homelessness, conducted basic needs assessments, and connected clients with housing, healthcare, and community resources. I have also worked with adults with disabilities in an individualized, strengths-based capacity, supporting independence, self-advocacy, and community engagement.
Currently, I am gaining additional clinical experience through my MSW internship at Washington Area Clinical Center, where I assist with treatment planning, quality assurance calls, patient follow-ups, clinical documentation, and observe intake assessments and patient-provider interactions. These experiences have expanded my interest in clinical social work and have motivated me to continue developing my skills in assessment, therapeutic engagement, and interdisciplinary care.
I am particularly interested in the opportunity to gain experience in both adolescent mental health and substance use recovery settings. I would welcome the opportunity to learn from the clinical teams at either Adolescent Wellness Academy or Principles Recovery Center and contribute to the meaningful work being done to support individuals and families. I value approaches grounded in empathy, collaboration, cultural humility, and an understanding of the unique experiences and strengths each client brings to the therapeutic process.
As I prepare for my relocation to South Florida, I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss potential January practicum openings, supervision availability, and the application process for either Davie location. I would be happy to provide additional information about my university's practicum requirements and coordinate with your team regarding placement expectations.
Thank you for your time and consideration,
Halie Fox

candidates.cover_letter:
I'm a Certified Behavioral Health Case Manager, with a Psychology degree from the University of Miami, and over three years of experience handling clinical file audits, insurance authorizations, and case management. I’d love to help keep your clients' care moving without delays as your company's new Utilization Review Specialist.

Right now, I work as a Housing Program Coordinator and Case Manager at Lotus House. My day-to-day is a mix of direct client support such as helping individuals manage depression and stabilize their health to heavy administrative review. I manage a high-volume caseload, verify Medicaid and Medicare coverage, run LOCUS risk assessments to track progress over time, and proactively audit clinical documentation to catch missing criteria before it leads to service or authorization delays. When denials do happen, I help clients and care teams navigate the gaps.

Before Lotus House, I worked remotely as a Compliance and Document Review Specialist for Miami-Dade County’s Emergency Rental Assistance Program, reviewing high-stakes applications against strict policy rules under tight deadlines. Between that, my research work at University of Miami, and daily EHR/HMIS tracking, I’m comfortable managing my own queue and staying organized while working remotely.

I’m familiar with DSM-5 and ASAM/LOCUS criteria, and I know how important clear, timely communication between clinical staff and insurance payers is for keeping treatment on track. Thank you so much for considering my application - I’d welcome the chance to talk more about how I can support your team!

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position with your PHP and IOP programs. As an art educator, experienced teacher, and graduate student in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a specialization in Play Therapy, I have built my career around exactly what this role describes: using creative, process-based experiences to help young people express themselves, regulate their emotions, and discover their own capacity to grow.

Over the past couple of years, I have taught process-based art to children and adolescents in a variety of settings. At artNEST Studios, I facilitated weekly after-school art programs for elementary students, designing curriculum that intentionally prioritized creative exploration over the final product. This approach gives participants permission to take risks, make mistakes, and express themselves authentically. I also managed full-cycle logistics for camps, workshops, and parties, adapting programming in real time to different group dynamics, ability levels, and unexpected challenges while maintaining safety standards. These experiences taught me how to read the room, keep a group engaged, and create a warm, inclusive environment where participants feel safe to participate fully.

My work extends beyond the art studio into clinical and crisis contexts. I served as a Volunteer Crisis Counselor with The Trevor Project, providing culturally competent crisis support to LGBTQ+ youth, and I currently volunteer with Harmonia, where my training in crisis de-escalation, harm reduction, and trauma-informed care allows me to provide on-site emotional support to individuals experiencing acute psychological distress.

What draws me most to AWA is the belief that growth happens through connection, creativity, and kindness. I have seen firsthand how a safe space to create can open the door to emotional expression for young people who struggle to put their feelings into words. I would be honored to bring my experience in art facilitation, group management, and trauma-informed support to adolescents in your program, and I can offer consistent weekly or biweekly availability for on-site groups.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my creative practice and clinical training can contribute to your organization.

Warm regards,
Natalia Perez

Shamaiah Manriquez
South Florida
331-250-1652
ShamaiahM@Gmail.com

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. My clinical experience also includes working with adolescents at Family First and with young adults at New Directions for Young Adults, where I facilitated therapeutic groups focused on emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, coping skills, and personal growth. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring my experience, compassion, and dedication to your team. I am eager to continue growing in the mental health field while helping adolescents feel heard, supported, and empowered throughout their journey.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With over five years of healthcare administrative experience and a deep commitment to compassionate patient advocacy, I am eager to bring my skills in insurance verification, electronic health records (EHR) management, and high-volume virtual support to your admissions team.

My daily responsibilities include verifying insurance eligibility, coordinating procedure benefits using ICD-10 and CPT coding, managing medical records requests, and scheduling appointments in high-volume clinical settings. Having managed these processes within Epic EHR while strictly upholding HIPAA compliance, I understand how critical speed, empathy, and precision are when families are seeking urgent behavioral health or substance use support.
Prior to CHRISTUS Health, my role as a Customer Service Representative at LINCARE Enteral Services honed my ability to coordinate care remotely across external agencies, verify coverage, and ensure timely documentation for critical patient needs. Additionally, my six years of service as a Correctional Officer with the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) equipped me to remain composed under pressure, de-escalate sensitive situations, and maintain meticulous, compliance-focused records. Together, these experiences allow me to support anxious parents and adolescents with both genuine warmth and operational reliability.
I am highly proficient in virtual communication and administrative tools, including Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Excel, and Workday, making me well-prepared to thrive in a remote admissions environment. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in patient intake, insurance verification, and crisis-ready communication can help families smoothly transition into your care programs.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely, 

Haley Ortega

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Thank you for following up on my application for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. What drew me to this role is the chance to help a family make sense of their options on the first call. When someone is worried about their teen, it matters that the person on the other end listens, explains what to expect, and makes it clear what happens next.

As a remote Benefits Counselor at Aon, I help employees work through questions about health coverage, eligibility, and enrollment. When someone isn’t sure what their plan covers, I ask what they’re trying to figure out, check the relevant plan details, and explain what they can do next in plain language. That work has taught me to be precise about what I can confirm, especially when someone is counting on the answer to make a decision.

At CVS, I answered pharmacy calls and helped patients at the counter while balancing the demands of a busy shift. I learned to stay patient when someone was frustrated, recognize when a question needed the pharmacist’s attention, and give a clear handoff. As a shift supervisor, I also trained 10 employees on store procedures and accurate recordkeeping. Those experiences would serve me well in admissions, where the details from one call can determine how smoothly the next step goes.

I’d bring that same care to answering inquiries, helping families understand the intake process, and following up so they know where things stand. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my benefits and pharmacy experience could support your admissions team.

Best,

Aarti Bala

Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator — Remote

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. My career has been spent in substance use treatment, behavioral health, and care coordination — doing intake, guiding people toward treatment, and being the first steady voice for families making a hard call. I would bring that same calm, follow-through approach to your admissions team.

The core of this role is work I already do. As an Addiction Management Specialist with Harrison Family Practice, I worked in medication-assisted treatment — documenting in EMR systems, handling prior authorizations, and supporting patients through long-term care plans. As a Case Manager with the Post Overdose Response Team, I connected people to treatment daily, coordinating detox placement and transportation and working directly with individuals and families in crisis. As a Community Navigator with The Columbus Organization, I managed a caseload of more than 45 individuals under a state-funded Medicaid waiver program, working majority remote, coordinating services between families, providers, and medical teams and explaining complex rules in plain, step-by-step terms. As a Scheduling Coordinator with Bridgeview Eye / Midwest Eye, I managed multiple incoming phone lines, scheduled appointments, and conducted triage intakes. In my current role as an Eligibility Specialist with Indiana FSSA, I verify eligibility and explain benefits to people daily.

I know the first call is often the hardest one a family makes. People reaching out about treatment are usually scared or exhausted, and they need someone who listens first, explains options plainly, and follows through. I have spent my career doing exactly that: staying calm with distressed callers, screening carefully, documenting accurately, and knowing when a situation needs the clinical team. I take confidentiality seriously and have worked with protected health information under HIPAA throughout my career. I learn new EMR and CRM systems quickly, and I have a dedicated home workspace set up for remote work.

I would welcome the chance to help Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center guide people and families into care. Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,

Bre Benner-Smith

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, administrative strengths, and patient-centered approach to the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my experience and skills can contribute to your admissions team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,

Morgan E. Kendrix

candidates.cover_letter:
Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to apply for a position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. Your work with teens ages 13–17 and their families, through intensive outpatient, partial hospitalization, therapeutic day, and after-school programs that keep adolescents connected to home and school, is exactly the kind of mental health care I want to build my career around.
My background in psychology at the University of Massachusetts Amherst gave me a strong foundation, and my most recent clinical experience put it into practice. As a Mental Health Specialist at Franciscan Children's, I worked with inpatient psychiatric patients and their care teams to plan for safe, successful discharge. That work showed me how much a young person's progress depends on steady communication between clinicians, families, and the community, which is the same model AWA uses to help teens heal without being pulled away from their daily lives.
Since the summer of 2019, I have volunteered at Hope House and Yawkey House of Possibilities, supporting children and adults with disabilities and serving as a Start Strong leader. Those years taught me patience, empathy, and how to meet people where they are. My interest in youth mental health started even earlier, through Buddies Club in high school and the Salem State Mental Health Advisory Week.
I currently work as a Human Resources Business Partner at MetricStream, where I support employees through sensitive situations, keep confidential records accurate, and communicate clearly with managers and staff. Reliability, discretion, and attention to detail are central to how I work, and I know they matter just as much in a treatment setting.
I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can contribute to you.

candidates.cover_letter:
Director or Supervisor,

My name is Meghan Reichardt-Nguyen and I feel that I can bring a wealth of knowledge and experience to this position. I completed a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling with a Specialization in Forensic Counseling from Walden University in May 2018. I maintained a 3.8 GPA throughout all my coursework, and I gained an immense amount of knowledge from the process. While completing my degree I regularly used Microsoft Office Programs as well as several different research/search databases.

In my most recent employment, I was employed with Behavioral Health Resources as a Substance Use Disorder and Co-Occurring Disorder Counselor. I worked with pregnant and parenting women experiencing substance use and co-occurring mental health symptoms. My responsibilities are to facilitate the Relapse Prevention Group, Anger Management Group,  Trauma Support Group and Parenting Group; as well as conduct weekly individual sessions with my assigned clients. I managed each client’s individualized treatment plan and collaborated with the client’s extended care teams to ensure the best support and care for the client. I supported medication management and documentation. I am responsible for documenting all client interactions during group sessions, individual sessions and legal proceedings and/or phone calls I witness or participate in. I also would complete the intake/admission process with eat client. I would ensure that all paperwork was completed and submitted to our clerk for each client. Furthermore, each month I would submit re-authorization to the client’s insurance companies so the clients could continue treatment. I conscientiously maintained HIPAA during every interaction with third party resources. The goal of this program is to help the client learn health coping skills, create a relapse prevention plan, maintain sobriety, and reunify with their children.

Previously I was employed with Rocky Mountain Crisis Partners as a Follow Up Specialist and a Crisis Specialist. I was responsible for making follow up calls for people experiencing crisis and/or people who have been recently discharged from the hospital following a crisis/event. I regularly dialed over 60+ calls daily and sometimes upwards of 100 dials on occasions. I collaborated with my fellow follow up specialists and crisis specialists to answer questions regarding follow ups, minimum standard of care procedures and research regarding pending follow ups. During these calls, I was able to help callers set goals, find mental health resources like care providers, and check in on their safety. Likewise, during these calls, I was able to help collaborate with the callers and help the callers determine the next course of action that is best for them. Once completing the calls, I completed documentation including three-part identification verification, the consents of the call and directions for the next call. Each call was tailored based on the needs of the caller and would be most helpful for them. I also occasionally received crisis calls from the crisis line as well. During these calls, I worked with callers to assess safety, determine the callers’ needs, and offer appropriate support. The goal when working with callers is to maintain the caller’s safety and support them through the crisis event they were experiencing at the time.

During my prior employment, I worked as an Assessment Specialist/Clinical Advisor. My duties included completing biopsychosocial assessments prior to admission into an Eating Disorder Program and maintaining HIPAA guidelines and regulations. I would gather the information from the client and input the data into Salesforce. These assessments were completed virtually via Ring Central and were used as a component to determine if a client was appropriate for our program and the appropriate level of care. I would also work with my team to ensure the client had completed all aspects of the admissions process prior to admitting to a program or level of care. I was tasked with providing the recommended level of care for each client I assessed. I would also request and process the release of information forms from clients. Furthermore, I have also worked in a group home named Haven House as an Associate Counselor. While working in this position, I worked with youths that had been displaced from their homes and places in foster care. I could gain insight into the foster care system in our state as well as the juvenile justice system from the perspective of a juvenile that has gone through the system. I have also worked with children with Autism when I was a Behavioral Interventionist when I worked at Aces-ABA. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With more than 15 years of experience across mortgage services, general management, and the service industry, I bring a strong foundation in communication, organization, relationship-building, and compassionate client support. More importantly, I bring a personal understanding of how deeply mental health and addiction can affect individuals, families, and entire communities.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed the ability to connect with people from all walks of life, listen to their needs, navigate challenging conversations, and help guide them through important decisions. My background in mortgage services has taught me the importance of patience, attention to detail, and helping people navigate complicated and sometimes stressful circumstances. My management and service industry experience have strengthened my ability to multitask, communicate effectively, remain composed under pressure, and make people feel heard and valued.

My interest in this position is also deeply personal. I have navigated my own mental health journey and have had the privilege of knowing many people who have fought through addiction and pursued sobriety. Recently, I experienced the heartbreaking loss of my best friend of 23 years to an overdose. Their struggle with addiction was deeply connected to childhood trauma and abuse. That loss has reinforced my belief that early intervention, compassionate support, and access to the right resources can make a life-changing difference.

I know firsthand that behind every struggle is a person deserving of understanding, dignity, and the opportunity for a better future. I would be honored to play a part in helping adolescents and their families find hope, access meaningful treatment, and recognize that their circumstances today do not have to define their tomorrow. Finding a future worth living for is something I believe everyone deserves the opportunity to experience.

I understand that an Admissions Coordinator is often one of the first points of contact for families navigating some of the most difficult and emotional moments of their lives. I would approach that responsibility with empathy, professionalism, patience, and genuine care. I believe my professional background, interpersonal strengths, and personal perspective would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your team and the families you serve.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how my experience, dedication, and passion for helping others could contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I would be proud to help make a difference in the lives of young people and help families find a path forward when they need it most.

Warm regards,

Reid L Golding
(512)656-3230
reidlgolding@gmail.com

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am reaching out because I would love the opportunity to join your team. For the past twelve years, my work and life have centered around supporting young people and their families through education, psychology and community work. When I came across this opening at Adolescent Wellness Academy, it immediately caught my attention because it aligns so closely with what I already care about and do every day.
Working in schools and special education for over a decade has taught me how to stay calm, adapt on the fly and truly connect with kids and teens from all walks of life. Alongside my classroom experience, my studies in clinical psychology and applied behavior analysis have helped me better understand what drives behavior and how to support youth through tough moments. Outside of work, I spend a lot of my time organizing local community outreach, mentorship, and family support efforts. I genuinely enjoy meeting new people, hearing their stories, and helping them figure out their next steps.
That same mindset carries over into my customer service background. Whether I am talking to a parent who feels overwhelmed, answering questions for a family, or working alongside a team, I always try to bring warmth, patience, and a steady presence to the room. People tend to feel comfortable opening up to me, and I take pride in making sure they feel heard and supported.
I also want to be completely honest about my administrative background. I have not worked directly in insurance billing before, though I do have plenty of experience writing detailed session notes specifically geared toward insurance billing requirements. candidates.cover_letter:
To Whom concern ,

I'm excited to apply for the Virtual admissions  coordinator position. Customer service isn’t about finishing a task, it’s about making sure a client gets the answers, the care, or the help they're waiting on. That's the mindset I've brought to every role I've held, and it's why I think I'd be a strong fit for your team.
At Elevance Health, I work directly with both members and providers for behavioral health and substance use services.  When a provider calls to check a claim  status, I dig into why it may have been denied and walk them through what’s needed to get it reprocessed correctly. 
Not just closing a ticket but actually solving the problem. On the member side, I've helped patients get referrals for mental health support  and stepped in when someone was running low on medication and needed a fast solution. Handling this kind of information comes with real responsibility, and I've kept HIPAA compliance and confidentiality at the center of everything I do.
My time as a Pharmacy Benefit Manager at TTEC built on that same foundation — verifying prescriptions, resolving access barriers, and making sure members understood their options, especially when cost or coverage issues got in the way. Between both roles, I've learned how to stay patient and clear with someone who's frustrated, how to track down the "why" behind a denial, and how to follow through until the issue is actually resolved.
What I'd bring to this role is simple: I listen first, I know how to navigate EOB, claims ,referrals  and coverage details without losing sight of the person on the other end, and I don't consider a case done until it's actually taken care of. I'd welcome the chance to bring that same care to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,

Kiana Dixon-C.

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With a diverse professional background in behavioral health administration, client relations, operations management, and remote customer service, I believe I bring a valuable combination of experience, compassion, and organizational skills that would make me a strong addition to your team.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my behavioral health experience with my passion for helping individuals and families navigate the process of accessing care. Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, experience in healthcare-related administrative support, patient eligibility, bilingual communication, and customer service, I believe I can bring valuable organizational and interpersonal skills to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and dedication could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Natasha L Mercado Ruiz

I am writing to express my interest in the remote position supporting adolescents experiencing mental health
challenges. With over six years of experience in healthcare, caregiving, behavioral health support, and
customer service, I have developed strong communication, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills that I
believe would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your team.

exposure to individuals experiencing mental health and behavioral challenges. In that role, I assisted with
providing support, monitoring changes in behavior, communicating concerns to appropriate staff, and using
de-escalation techniques while prioritizing individual dignity and safety.
In my current role as an Operations Manager in home healthcare, I serve as a primary point of contact for
clients, families, caregivers, and prospective employees. I regularly handle sensitive conversations, address
concerns, coordinate services, maintain confidential records, and help individuals navigate challenging
situations. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, remain
composed under pressure, and provide dependable support in a fast-paced environment.
I am particularly interested in this opportunity because I value the importance of mental health support and
understand how meaningful it can be when individuals feel heard, respected, and supported. I would
welcome the opportunity to use my healthcare background, behavioral health experience, and administrative
skills to help adolescents and their families navigate the resources and support available to them.
I also hold a Bachelor of Business Administration with a focus in Healthcare, which has provided me with a
strong foundation in healthcare operations and professional communication. I am comfortable working with
multiple administrative systems, managing competing priorities, documenting information accurately, and
communicating effectively in a remote or team-based environment.
Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience,
professionalism, and commitment to compassionate service could contribute to your organization. I look
forward to the possibility of joining your team.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am confident that my healthcare background, strong work ethic, ability to manage multiple responsibilities, and genuine passion for helping others would allow me to contribute positively to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills align with your team's needs.

Sincerely,  
Krystal Silva

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than 15 years of experience in Christian ministry, including biblical counseling, recovery support, program coordination, and client services, I would welcome the opportunity to help individuals and families take meaningful steps toward receiving the care they need.

As Founder and Co-Director of Mourning Dove Discipleship Counseling, Inc., I have worked with individuals and families facing challenging circumstances, including substance use and recovery-related concerns. My experience includes conducting initial conversations, assessing individual needs within the scope of my role, maintaining confidential records, coordinating referrals, and helping individuals identify appropriate recovery resources.

My work with Capstone Recovery Center and Bethel Colony has further strengthened my understanding of the challenges individuals face when seeking recovery services. I recognize the importance of listening carefully, communicating compassionately, and providing clear, practical guidance during what may be an overwhelming time.

In addition to my ministry experience, I bring more than 25 years of experience in financial services, where accuracy, confidentiality, regulatory compliance, client communication, and timely follow-through were essential. I am comfortable learning new technology, maintaining databases, managing multiple responsibilities, and working independently. I have also developed and maintained a searchable database of Christ-centered recovery resources to assist individuals and organizations in locating appropriate services.

What particularly attracts me to this position is the opportunity to serve as a compassionate and dependable first point of contact for individuals and families seeking help. I understand that the initial conversation can influence whether someone feels comfortable taking the next step, and I would approach that responsibility with patience, professionalism, and genuine concern.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience in recovery support, client services, and administration could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Barbara Benfield

Sincerely,

Kendall Eddings

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,
I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I should be upfront about two gaps: my admissions work has been in a children's services program rather than a treatment program, and I haven't worked fully remote. I'm applying because the heart of this job is helping someone through a hard day and making sure they leave the call with a clear next step, and that is work I already do.
At PMS Children Services, I enroll families into our program, take their calls, answer their questions, and follow up until the next step actually happens. I keep case documentation accurate and confidential. Before that, at Behavior Change Institute, I worked one-on-one with children and adults with autism and related disabilities, carried out their behavior plans as written, and kept clinical records under HIPAA. My psychology degree and my Family Engagement Credentialed Administrator credential back up that experience.
Your posting asks for someone who can explain PHP and IOP in plain, caring language. On the phone with families, I explain things in plain terms to people who are tired, worried, or new to the process, and I've learned to stay calm and warm while I do it. I'm also used to working through my own caseload, so I expect the day-to-day rhythm of managing a pipeline to feel familiar.
I'm ready to learn your CRM, your EMR, and the insurance verification process, and I follow written procedures closely, which matters in work that has to be HIPAA-compliant.
Thank you for considering my application. I'd welcome the chance to talk with you.
Sincerely,
Mario Thomas

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. Having walked alongside two of my own children through complex mental health and substance use challenges—including the loss of one of my children this past January—I know firsthand how vital compassionate, accessible, and family-centered care truly is.

Professionally, I pair that understanding with reliability, discretion, and organizational focus to ensure daily operations run smoothly so clinicians and families can focus on healing.

My key strengths include:
•	Empathetic Family Support: Lived understanding of the emotional realities facing parents and adolescents navigating mental health and substance use recovery, paired with a warm, nonjudgmental demeanor.
•	Calm Under Pressure: Proven ability to remain steady, compassionate, and resourceful in high-stress or sensitive situations while maintaining clear professional boundaries.
•	Administrative & Client Service Excellence: Experienced in scheduling, managing confidential records with strict respect for privacy, coordinating communications, and creating an organized, welcoming environment.

While my personal journey has shaped my heart for this work, my professional experience equips me to contribute reliably and effectively to your team from day one.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and dedication can support the families you serve.

Warm regards, 
Phillippa Campbell

Ericka Harris

I bring a diverse professional background in human services, victim advocacy, forensic interviewing, business operations, and team leadership, along with a genuine passion for helping others and making a meaningful difference in the lives of those I serve.

Throughout my career, I have developed strong skills in communication, problem-solving, crisis response, client support, organization, and collaboration. My experience working with individuals and families in vulnerable or challenging circumstances has strengthened my ability to approach situations with compassion, professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment.

In my current role as a Victim Advocate and Forensic Interviewer, I provide trauma-informed support, conduct child-centered forensic interviews, coordinate with multidisciplinary professionals, connect families with resources, and help individuals navigate complex systems. I am ChildFirst® trained/certified and have completed more than 60 specialized professional training courses covering areas such as mental health, human trafficking, disability services, and support for older adults, in addition to more than 40 hours of victim advocacy training.

My previous experience with the Kansas Department for Children and Families, combined with my background in management, administration, and customer service, has given me a well-rounded understanding of both direct client services and organizational operations. I hold an Associate Degree in Business Management and bring an ability to adapt quickly, take initiative, work independently, and contribute positively to a team.

I am looking for an opportunity where I can continue growing professionally while bringing my experience, work ethic, compassion, and dedication to an organization that values its employees and the people it serves. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and abilities could contribute to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you.

Sincerely,

Dezarae Whelchel

November 19, 2026
Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Team,

When a family calls about a teenager who is struggling, the first voice they hear shapes whether they take the next step. I would welcome the chance to be that voice as your Virtual Admissions Coordinator. Over more than ten years in healthcare and office management, my work has centered on the same things this role asks for: walking people through difficult decisions with warmth and clarity, handling insurance details accurately, and keeping a full pipeline moving without letting anyone slip through the cracks.

At Aspen Dental, I reviewed treatment plans directly with patients, many of whom were anxious about cost, coverage, or the care itself. I learned to listen first, explain options plainly, and help people feel confident enough to commit to treatment. I consistently exceeded monthly performance goals, earned the CEO's Wisdom Tooth Award, and was promoted to National Trainer for Office Managers. I also handled scheduling and patient flow for a busy practice, so I understand how intake, follow-up, and timing affect whether someone actually starts care.

Before that, as a Cash Application Specialist at Providence Health and Services, I reconciled insurance payments line by line against Explanation of Benefits documents. That work gave me a solid grounding in how coverage and benefits are applied, along with a strong habit of accurate, confidential documentation in a HIPAA environment.

Since 2021, I have been Office Manager at Mountainview Contractors, where I run payroll, reconcile all banking, order materials, and coordinate schedules, largely on my own. I'm used to setting my own priorities, following up without being reminded, and keeping clean records every day. These are the habits a remote admissions role depends on.

I haven't worked in substance use admissions yet, and I'm eager to learn your PHP and IOP programs, your CRM, and your intake process thoroughly. What I bring is a proven ability to build trust quickly over the phone, meet goals, and treat every caller with dignity. Families reaching out for an adolescent are often at their most overwhelmed, and I would be proud to help them feel heard and guided toward care.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to talk about how I can support your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Brittany Froelich

candidates.cover_letter:
Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Team,

Many people call a treatment program on the hardest day of their lives. I know that because I have been the person making those calls. I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I can bring both professional healthcare coordination experience and a family perspective on what a caller needs from the first conversation.

In my family, I have helped coordinate care for a loved one living with schizophrenia, and I have supported family members through substance use. That meant finding the right providers, understanding insurance and what it would cover, keeping appointments and paperwork on track, and staying steady and patient when things were hard. It taught me to listen without judgment, explain next steps in plain language, and follow up until someone is connected to care. These are the skills your role asks for, and I use them every day.

Professionally, I have more than 14 years in healthcare administration. At Thrive Therapeutic Services, I worked fully remote in a mental health practice, handling patient registration, insurance verification, claims, and the schedules of more than ten therapists, with confidential, accurate records. At Mission Medical, I coordinated referrals for medications, procedures, and inpatient and outpatient mental health services. I also completed prior authorizations and worked daily with insurers, nurse case managers, and pharmacies. At Johnson’s Orthopedic, I verified primary, secondary, and tertiary benefits through multiple payer portals. At MRO Corp., I handled escalated calls from patients and providers and supervise a team.

I am comfortable working independently without daily direction, managing my own follow-up, and documenting every contact in an EMR (I have used Epic, TherapyNotes, and others) in a HIPAA-compliant way. I would welcome the chance to be a calm, caring first voice for the teens, adults, and families your programs serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would be glad to talk about how I can support your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Andrea Miracle

Taylor Williams

I am excited to submit my application for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. After reviewing the responsibilities and qualifications for this role, I immediately recognized how closely they align with my professional experience, skill set, and passion for healthcare administration.

I also have specific experience reviewing insurance benefits and authorization requirements for Partial Hospitalization Programs (PHP) and Intensive Outpatient Programs (IOP), making me particularly familiar with an important aspect of this position. My experience navigating insurance portals, working within multiple EMR systems, managing documentation, and communicating with various healthcare professionals has prepared me to contribute effectively to your admissions team.

I understand that the admissions process can be an important and sometimes overwhelming first step for individuals and families seeking treatment. I believe clear communication, compassion, attention to detail, and consistent follow-through are essential when helping families navigate their options and access the care they need. I would welcome the opportunity to bring those qualities, along with my healthcare experience, to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines my existing experience with the ability to contribute to a team in a virtual healthcare setting. I am confident that my background and familiarity with the responsibilities of this position would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with the needs of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to hearing from you.

Chantilly McKinnon

Sherman, Texas

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor’s degree in social work and professional experience as an Eligibility Specialist with the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC), I bring a strong background in client advocacy, service coordination, eligibility screening, confidential documentation, and connecting individuals and families with essential resources.

In my current role with HHSC, I work directly with individuals and families navigating complex and often stressful circumstances. I regularly assess individual needs, gather and evaluate sensitive information, explain eligibility requirements and available services, maintain accurate case documentation, and help individuals navigate systems that can otherwise feel overwhelming. This experience has strengthened my ability to communicate with compassion, exercise sound judgment, manage competing priorities, and ensure that people feel heard and supported throughout the process.

My educational background in social work has further developed my understanding of mental health, substance use, family dynamics, crisis situations, and the importance of meeting individuals where they are. I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of its focus on helping adolescents and families access mental health treatment, as well as supporting individuals seeking recovery from substance use disorders. I believe that the first interaction someone has with a treatment provider can make a meaningful difference in whether they feel comfortable taking that next step toward receiving help.

I would bring a combination of empathy, professionalism, organization, and strong follow-through to your admissions team. I am comfortable handling sensitive conversations, gathering detailed information, maintaining confidentiality, navigating complex administrative processes, and communicating information in a way that is clear and approachable. I also understand the importance of accurate documentation, timely follow-up, and treating every individual and family with dignity and respect.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my social work education, public service experience, and passion for helping individuals and families to your organization. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and skills could contribute to your admissions team and the individuals you serve.

Sincerely,

Chantilly McKinnon

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Application for Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness
Academy. I am eager to bring my healthcare customer service experience, communication skills, and educational
background to your team. I am especially interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to support the
process of connecting adolescents and families with services and care.
I hold an Associate degree in General Studies from Delgado Community College. During my college studies, I
completed coursework in psychology and sociology, including two levels of sociology and introductory psychology
coursework focused on understanding the human mind and behavior. These classes strengthened my interest in
how people think, learn, interact, and are influenced by the environments around them. I believe this academic
foundation, together with my professional experience, would be valuable when communicating respectfully with
individuals and families who may be navigating difficult or unfamiliar situations.
In my member services role with CVS Health/Aetna, I handled inbound calls, listened to members’ concerns,
communicated information clearly, and helped people navigate healthcare-related questions. This experience
strengthened my ability to remain patient, professional, and composed in a fast-paced environment. It also taught
me the importance of listening carefully, protecting sensitive information, following procedures, and making sure
each caller feels heard and respected.
My experience at Planet Fitness further developed my customer service and communication abilities. I assisted
members, answered questions, handled phone and computer-related tasks, and supported daily operations.
Across these roles, I learned to build rapport, stay organized, adapt to different personalities, and follow through
when someone needs assistance.
While my professional background is in customer service and healthcare member support rather than clinical
admissions, I am ready and willing to learn your organization’s admissions procedures, systems, and
expectations. I would approach conversations with adolescents and families with empathy and professionalism,
follow established guidelines, and seek guidance whenever a situation requires it. I understand that this role
carries responsibility, and I would take that responsibility seriously.
I am seeking an opportunity where I can contribute, continue learning, and grow professionally. I would be grateful
for the chance to discuss how my associate degree, psychology and sociology coursework, and customer service

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining Adolescent Wellness Academy. Throughout my career, I have been drawn to work that allows me to support individuals through difficult circumstances, advocate for their needs, and help them build confidence, independence, and a stronger sense of belonging.

I bring over a decade of experience as a Direct Support Professional, along with a background in healthcare-related administration, quality assurance, program coordination, and operations. During my years with La Rue's Community Care, I supported individuals with diverse developmental, behavioral, and medical needs. My responsibilities included individualized care planning, daily documentation, monitoring changes in health and behavior, communicating with families, and maintaining compliance with established care standards.

These experiences taught me that meaningful support begins with trust. I understand the importance of meeting individuals where they are, recognizing the reasons behind challenging behaviors, maintaining appropriate boundaries, and creating an environment where people feel safe, respected, and understood.

As a parent of two teenagers, I also recognize the unique challenges adolescents face as they develop their identities, navigate relationships, and learn to manage their emotions. I believe young people benefit tremendously from consistent adults who listen without judgment, provide encouragement, and help them recognize their own strengths.

My additional experience in recruiting, operations, and program administration has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively, manage competing priorities, maintain confidential records, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to contribute to an environment focused on the emotional well-being, personal growth, and long-term success of young people. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my compassion, professional experience, reliability, and commitment to person-centered care to your team.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and dedication to supporting individuals and families align with your organization's needs.

Sincerely,

Nancy Sutherland

Victoria Kinney

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with your organization. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to a team that helps adolescents and families navigate the process of receiving mental health and substance use treatment.

This experience has taught me the importance of patience, compassion, professionalism, and building trust with individuals and their families. I consider myself a highly motivated, dependable, and quick-learning individual who takes pride in being organized, approachable, and goal-oriented. I am comfortable working independently, managing multiple responsibilities, and communicating with people from different backgrounds. I would welcome the opportunity to bring these qualities to your admissions team and help make a positive difference for adolescents and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and dedication to helping others could make me a valuable addition to your team.


Sincerely,
Victoria Kinney

work_history.title: Senior Recovery Coach/Family Recovery Coach
work_history.company_name: Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery
work_history.summary: Certified CCAR Recovery Coach. Working on a peer to peer platform that is fully Recoveree based. I conduct meetings in office and out in the community. I help everyone from active addicts to those with 20+ years of sobriety, and I help them figure out "what is next". Stopping the use of substances is a monumentally positive achievement and very hard to maintain. That being said, life does not slow down before, during, or after active use. I am here to support and help any and all Recoverees no matter what stage they are at to make their lives manageable. I often get the question, "I stopped doing drugs, that is great, now what?" or "how do i fix all the issues I have created from my substance use?" and this is exactly where I come in as a Recovery Coach. Any and all questions I find answers for. If I cannot answer it myself I will find the appropriate person who can. It is also important to say that I actually do not DO any of the work for a Recoveree. They do all the work themselves, and I just provide guidance and tools. There's no mandatory ANYTHING with Recovery Coaching and that is how we meet the Recoveree where they are at. The recoveree creates a Wellness Plan with me and we track progress towards eat goal no matter what it is or how big or how small the progress might be. All of this while retraining the brain to ditch the "instant Gratification" mind set and molding a positive and personable personal atmosphere. There is no such thing as failure unless you give up and I am here to try anything and everything to get a person where they really want to be and push past their idea of potential and into a whole new realm of what they can do. This also comes with Insurance auth/reauth services, Billing setups, intake/discharge documentation, avid computer skills for written documents, skills in the use of software for maintaining and organizing documentation, digital and paper documentation of all engagements, ESM Virtual Gateway Assessments for BSAS, communicating with other providers within the Recoveree's circle for integrated care, communicating with insurance companies to continue engagement in services, following HIPPA and 42 CFR guidelines and filling out appropriate Release Documentation, and all other forms and documentation required for confidentiality, referrals, and insurance/billing. I also possess logins for the Executive Office of Health and Human Services, and all insurance companies under the MA Health umbrella. I report to a supervisor who previously had my position but is now the Director of a Peer Center owned and operated by LHI and funded by BSAS so I am the only member of my department not in management. I was tasked with writing the entire operational process from start to finish, meeting a client for the first time to discharging after completion, and ALL the processes in-between. This includes the billing, insurance, contact documentation, filing forms for HIPPA and 42 CFR, all the guidelines for BSAS and MA Health Insurance. These book only pertains to the processes of Recovery Coaching specifically at Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery. I will be with Lowell House Addiction Treatment and Recovery for 2 years as of June 2021and hope to be promoted to the Recovery Coach Supervisor for all new interns and New Hires as they will be using the book I created to learn how to do the job. Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Throughout my career in counseling, education, caregiving, and client support, I have been dedicated to helping individuals and families navigate some of life's most difficult challenges with compassion, professionalism, and practical guidance. The opportunity to serve as the first point of contact for individuals seeking mental health and substance use treatment strongly aligns with both my experience and my passion for helping others access needed support.

As a school counselor and student services counselor, I regularly worked with students and families facing behavioral health concerns, substance abuse issues, crisis situations, grief, homelessness, family conflict, and mental health challenges. I conducted needs assessments, provided crisis intervention, coordinated referrals to community resources and mental health providers, maintained detailed documentation, and collaborated with multidisciplinary teams to ensure appropriate support services were in place.

During my graduate counseling training, I completed an internship at Roots Renewal Ranch, an inpatient treatment program serving adolescent girls experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. In this role, I worked closely with clients navigating complex emotional, behavioral, and recovery-related concerns while collaborating with clinical staff to support treatment goals and overall well-being. This experience provided me with valuable insight into the treatment continuum, the courage required to seek help, and the importance of creating a supportive, nonjudgmental environment for clients and their families. It also strengthened my understanding of the unique needs of adolescents in treatment and reinforced my commitment to helping individuals access the services and support necessary for lasting recovery.

In addition to my counseling background, I recently served as the primary caregiver for a family member living with dementia, coordinating healthcare services, appointments, communication among providers, and ongoing care planning. This experience further strengthened my ability to remain organized, responsive, compassionate, and solution-focused during emotionally difficult circumstances. I have also recently returned to direct caregiving work within an assisted living setting, reinforcing my commitment to supporting individuals during vulnerable periods of their lives.

What attracts me most to AWA and PRC is your commitment to meeting individuals and families with empathy during critical moments. I understand that reaching out for help often requires tremendous courage. I would welcome the opportunity to provide the calm, supportive guidance that helps callers feel heard, informed, and confident in taking their next step toward treatment.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my counseling, care coordination, and family advocacy experience can contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Joanne Phillips

I am currently completing my Master's degree in School Counseling with LPC, through which I have gained valuable, hands-on experience supporting adolescents and their families through various situations and challenges across educational and behavioral health settings. In my school counseling practicum at Winfree Academy (a drop-out recovery charter school system) and my counsleing role at Pilot Point ISD, I provided individual and small-group counseling, conducted student needs assessments, collaborated with families, multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders, assisted with crisis response, and connected students and families to appropriate academic, mental health, and community resources.

Most recently, I have served as a caregiver for both my elderly mother with dementia as well as another elderly client. candidates.cover_letter:
I am reaching out to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. I have attached my resume for your consideration.

Throughout my professional career, I have developed a strong background in administration, client relations, scheduling, data management, and working directly with individuals and families from diverse backgrounds. In my current role with a nonprofit organization, I work closely with community members, coordinate appointments and services, maintain records, and provide administrative support to executive leadership. Previously, as a business owner, I managed more than 1,000 clients and over 30 contractors, which required exceptional organization, communication, problem-solving, and the ability to handle sensitive situations with patience and professionalism.

I also have an educational background in secondary education, along with more than ten years of experience working with children and adolescents through school districts, student support roles, and youth coaching programs. These experiences have given me an appreciation for the importance of patience, understanding, and creating supportive environments for young people and their families.

I am currently exploring new professional opportunities due to changes in my personal circumstances that may make my current position less aligned with both the organization’s evolving needs and what I am able to offer moving forward. I am hoping to find a role where I can continue utilizing my administrative and interpersonal skills while contributing to work that has a meaningful impact on individuals and families.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because of the chance to support adolescents and their families during what can often be an overwhelming and difficult time. I would value the opportunity to be a compassionate and organized first point of contact, helping families navigate the admissions process and connect with the support and resources they need.

I would also be interested in learning more about the position’s remote work expectations, typical scheduling, and hours.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my professional background, communication skills, and passion for helping others could contribute to your team. I look forward to hearing from you!

Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator, Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. For more than two years, I have been the person families reach on the hardest day of their lives. I am a crisis receiving clinician at Charlotte Behavioral Health Care. I would like to bring that experience to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

I handle the full admissions process, from first contact to completed admission. I screen adults and children for mental health and substance use needs and decide whether they meet admission criteria. I gather collateral from families, providers, and law enforcement. I make sure every legal form is signed, understood, and entered accurately into the EMR in compliance with HIPAA. I also follow up with patients after screening. I am comfortable working remotely and independently. I serve as a remote on-call clinician twice weekly from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., handling admissions without direct supervision. Before that, I worked full-time as a remote medical scribe for University of Wisconsin Medical. I have extensive EMR experience with Meditech, Epic, MyChart, and SmartCare, and I learn new systems quickly. I speak intermediate Spanish.

Frightened callers need calm, plain language. My training in de-escalation and tactical communication helps me provide it. So does my background teaching about 500 college students, which taught me to explain complex information patiently. I would welcome the chance to bring this experience to your adolescent and adult programs.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how I can support your admissions team.

Sincerely, 

Michael P. Berte
