candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager, 

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a background in mental health services, clinical work, and program support, I bring a combination of administrative, organizational, and interpersonal skills that align well with the responsibilities of this role. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate the process of accessing mental health and substance use treatment during what can often be a difficult and overwhelming time.

In my previous role as a Program Support Specialist within Post-Release Services, I developed experience supporting program operations, coordinating services, maintaining documentation, and communicating with individuals and various service providers. This role strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, maintain organized records, facilitate communication, and ensure that important follow-up tasks were completed. Additionally, my clinical experience has provided me with familiarity with electronic health record systems, timely and accurate documentation, client scheduling, and the importance of maintaining confidentiality and HIPAA-compliant practices.

As a mental health professional, I understand the importance of approaching individuals and families with empathy, patience, and clear communication. I recognize that reaching out for treatment can be a vulnerable first step, particularly for adolescents and their families. I would bring a compassionate, nonjudgmental approach to initial inquiries while maintaining the organization, consistency, and attention to detail necessary to support an effective admissions process. I am also comfortable navigating conversations that require balancing sensitivity with clear communication, follow-through, and appropriate coordination of services.

Although my background has primarily been in clinical and program support settings rather than a dedicated admissions role, I believe these experiences have equipped me with highly transferable skills. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical perspective, administrative capabilities, and commitment to accessible mental health care to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skill set could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephanie Lee-Ferreira

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in medical administration and patient care, I have developed a genuine appreciation for the importance of compassionate communication, organization, and helping individuals navigate what can often be an overwhelming healthcare system.

In my previous role as a Medical Receptionist in a busy primary care practice, I was responsible for patient scheduling, insurance verification, coordinating referrals, managing patient communications, and maintaining accurate records through Epic EHR. I regularly assisted patients who were frustrated, confused, or anxious about their care, and I learned how important it is to approach each interaction with patience, empathy, and a willingness to find solutions.

Additionally, my experience as a full-time caregiver strengthened my ability to support individuals through vulnerable and challenging circumstances. These experiences have taught me to remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly, and recognize that even the smallest interactions can make a meaningful difference in someone's day.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the chance to be a supportive first point of contact for individuals and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment. I understand that reaching out for help can be an incredibly difficult step, and I would take pride in helping make that experience feel less intimidating and more reassuring. I am also drawn to the opportunity to work independently while remaining connected to a team dedicated to helping people access the care they need.

Although my professional background has primarily been in primary care rather than behavioral health admissions, I am confident that my experience with patient coordination, insurance processes, electronic health records, and sensitive patient interactions has prepared me to transition successfully into this role. I am eager to expand my knowledge of behavioral health services and contribute to a team making such an important difference in people's lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, work ethic, and commitment to compassionate patient care could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,  
Angela Balice

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in employment opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 10 years of experience in behavioral health, mental health services, program leadership, and supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am passionate about contributing to an organization dedicated to improving the emotional, behavioral, and overall well-being of young people.

Throughout my career, I have developed extensive experience in behavioral health program operations, team leadership, service coordination, family engagement, and quality improvement. In my current leadership role, I oversee program operations, support staff development, monitor performance outcomes, promote compliance with program requirements, and ensure that services are delivered with compassion, accountability, and a focus on individualized care. I have successfully rebuilt teams, strengthened operational processes, and exceeded performance expectations established by funders.

My professional philosophy centers on meeting adolescents where they are, recognizing their strengths, understanding their individual challenges, and providing the structure, support, and encouragement necessary for growth. I understand the importance of creating safe, supportive environments where young people feel heard, respected, and empowered to develop healthy coping skills, emotional regulation, confidence, and independence. I also recognize that meaningful progress often requires collaboration with families, schools, community partners, and multidisciplinary treatment teams.

I hold a Bachelor of Science degree and a Master of Healthcare Administration, and I am currently pursuing doctoral-level education in Public Health. My educational background, combined with my hands-on experience in behavioral health leadership, has strengthened my ability to approach adolescent wellness from both an operational and person-centered perspective.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my leadership experience, passion for youth advocacy, and commitment to behavioral health excellence to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am confident that my skills, professional values, and dedication to serving adolescents and families would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Dear Hiring Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the remote Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over 10 years of experience in healthcare, behavioral health support, and consumer relations, I specialize in guiding individuals and families through sensitive, high-stress decisions with warmth, clarity, and urgency. I deeply admire Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to providing compassionate, specialized mental health and substance use care for teens, and I would be honored to serve as a supportive first point of contact for your families.
Reaching out for adolescent treatment is often one of the most overwhelming moments a parent or guardian will ever face. Serving as a Virtual Admissions Coordinator requires more than administrative precision—it demands active listening, genuine empathy, and the ability to build immediate trust over the phone or screen. Throughout my career, I have developed a strong foundation in these exact areas:
• Empathetic Family & Client Rapport: Experienced in de-escalating crisis moments, listening without judgment, and reassuring anxious parents and caregivers while clearly explaining program options and next steps.
• Seamless Intake & Insurance Navigation: Skilled at conducting thorough initial assessments, verifying insurance benefits accurately, coordinating with clinical teams for level-of-care approvals, and maintaining strict HIPAA compliance in a remote environment.
• Persistent, Organized Follow-Through: Proven ability to manage a high volume of inquiries in CRM and EHR systems, ensuring timely follow-ups so no teen or family falls through the cracks during the critical window between first contact and admission.
Working remotely requires strong self-direction and seamless communication with multidisciplinary teams. My background bridging front-line support and healthcare administration allows me to collaborate effortlessly with clinicians, utilization review specialists, and outreach teams to ensure every transition into care is as smooth and stress-free as possible.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my dedication to behavioral health advocacy, rapport building, and admissions coordination can help Adolescent Wellness Academy connect more teens and families with life-changing care. I can be reached at 812-653-6468 or richardsonfancy@gmail.com to schedule an interview.  

With Gratitude 
Nancy M Richardson

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in Administrative opportunities with your organization. With several years of experience in customer service, office support, scheduling coordination, and client communication, I am eager to bring my professionalism, organization, and welcoming personality to a team where I can contribute and continue growing professionally.

Victoria Welch

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With six years of experience in healthcare, including roles as a Surgery Coordinator and Ophthalmic Scribe, I have developed a strong background in patient communication, care coordination, scheduling, and administrative support. I am confident that my experience, attention to detail, and compassionate approach to patient care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Throughout my time as a Surgery Coordinator, I served as a primary point of contact for patients navigating the surgical process. My responsibilities included coordinating procedures, managing schedules, communicating with patients and medical providers, and ensuring all necessary documentation and preoperative requirements were completed. I understand how overwhelming medical decisions can feel, and I take pride in helping patients feel informed, comfortable, and supported throughout their care.

My experience as an Ophthalmic Scribe has further strengthened my ability to manage detailed medical records, navigate electronic medical record systems, maintain patient confidentiality, and communicate effectively within a fast-paced healthcare environment. These roles have taught me the importance of organization, accuracy, adaptability, and consistent follow-through.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to be a reassuring first point of contact for individuals and families seeking help. While my professional background has primarily been in ophthalmology, I believe the compassion, patience, and communication skills I have developed are directly transferable to admissions coordination. I recognize that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly vulnerable experience, and I would approach every interaction with empathy, professionalism, and respect.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, organizational skills, and dedication to patient-centered care to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Victoria Welch

To Whom it May Concern:

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I am drawn to this opportunity because it combines strong administrative and organizational skills with something I deeply value: making mental health and substance use treatment more accessible to individuals and families who need support.

I bring strong administrative, communication, multitasking, and organizational skills, along with the ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and professionalism. I understand the importance of keeping information organized, maintaining detailed records, coordinating schedules, following up consistently, and ensuring that no important detail is overlooked. I take pride in being dependable, efficient, and proactive, and I understand the importance of managing responsibilities independently in a remote work environment.

What particularly interests me about this position is the opportunity to make a meaningful difference during what may be one of the most difficult times in someone's life. I believe mental health is just as important as physical health, and everyone deserves to feel heard, respected, and supported when reaching out for help. Whether speaking with a concerned parent, an individual struggling with substance use, or a healthcare provider making a referral, I would approach every interaction with compassion, patience, empathy, and professionalism.

I also recognize that the admissions process involves much more than answering phone calls. It requires excellent follow-through, clear communication, attention to confidentiality, accurate documentation, and the ability to coordinate multiple moving parts to help individuals access the care they need. I would bring a strong sense of responsibility to managing inquiries, coordinating assessments, assisting with paperwork, and ensuring that each person receives timely communication and guidance throughout the admissions process.

I would welcome the opportunity to combine my administrative abilities with my passion for supporting mental health and recovery. I admire the work both organizations are doing to provide individuals and families with access to treatment, and I would be proud to contribute to a team that helps people take meaningful steps toward healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my skills, work ethic, and commitment to compassionate service could benefit your admissions team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your organization's mission.

Sincerely,

Erica O’Brien

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With an extensive background in human services, substance-use counseling, client intake, program management, and advocacy, I bring a combination of experience that closely aligns with the needs of your admissions team.

My professional experience includes working as a Substance Abuse Counselor, supporting individuals facing substance-use challenges and helping connect them with appropriate services, resources, and recovery support. I also have direct intake experience in homeless services, where I conducted client intakes, gathered information, identified individual needs, and helped individuals navigate available services and support systems. These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the importance of listening without judgment, building trust, and helping people take the first steps toward meaningful change.

Additionally, I served as a Long-Term Care Ombudsman and Program Manager with Mother Lode Senior Services, advocating for vulnerable populations, addressing sensitive concerns, coordinating services, maintaining confidential records, and working with families and service providers. I also performed Ombudsman responsibilities remotely, developing the independence, communication, organization, and follow-through necessary to work effectively in a virtual environment.

Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals and families experiencing difficult and often overwhelming circumstances. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance-use treatment can be an emotional and sometimes difficult decision. I believe the first interaction can make a lasting impression, and I would approach every caller with compassion, professionalism, patience, and respect.

I am highly organized, dependable, comfortable managing multiple priorities, and experienced in handling sensitive information and documentation. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my counseling, intake, advocacy, and program coordination experience to your team and help individuals and families navigate the admissions process with confidence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,

Jill Engle

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. This opportunity immediately stood out to me because it combines my professional experience working with vulnerable youth and my personal passion for mental health, substance use recovery, and helping young people find their way forward.

Previously, I worked as a Youth Advocate with Windsor County Youth Services, supporting young people facing difficult circumstances. I also have experience in housing case management, crisis intervention, coordinating services, and helping individuals access the resources they need. These roles strengthened my communication skills, compassion, and ability to connect with individuals during some of their most challenging moments.

What makes this position especially meaningful to me is that my connection to youth services goes beyond my professional experience. As a young teenager, I was once a client of youth services myself. I experienced my own struggles with mental health and addiction, and I understand firsthand how overwhelming those challenges can be, particularly at such a young age. I also understand how much of a difference it can make when someone takes the time to listen without judgment, offer guidance, and genuinely advocate for your well-being.

Having experienced both sides of youth services—as someone who once needed support and later became someone providing it—I bring a unique perspective to this work. My experiences have given me a deep sense of empathy, resilience, and a genuine desire to help adolescents and their families navigate the treatment process.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. My professional background includes working as an ABA therapist, respite care worker, after-school teacher, and nanny. Through these roles, I have developed a strong foundation in behavioral support, communication, relationship-building, and providing compassionate care to individuals and families navigating challenging circumstances.

As an ABA therapist, I gained hands-on experience supporting individuals with behavioral and developmental needs, implementing individualized strategies, and communicating with families to support meaningful progress. My experience as a respite worker further strengthened my ability to provide dependable, individualized care while understanding the unique challenges families face. Working as an after-school teacher and nanny also taught me how to build trust quickly, manage competing needs, maintain structure, and create safe and supportive environments for children.

What draws me to this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference before someone even begins treatment. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use support can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience for individuals and their families. I would approach every interaction with patience, empathy, professionalism, and the understanding that the first conversation can have a lasting impact on someone's willingness to seek help.

I bring strong interpersonal skills, attention to detail, adaptability, and a genuine passion for helping others. I am comfortable working independently, managing responsibilities, communicating with diverse families, and following through to ensure people feel supported throughout a process. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my hands-on behavioral health and caregiving experience into an admissions setting and continue growing professionally in this field.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would love the opportunity to discuss how my experience and passion for supporting individuals and families could contribute to your team.

Dear Hiring Manager,
     I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With a Bachelor of Science in Psychology, a Master of Science in Criminal Behavioral Studies, and a strong interest in behavioral health, I am eager to contribute to an organization dedicated to helping adolescents and their families access appropriate treatment and support.

My educational background has provided me with a strong foundation in psychological principles, behavioral health, crisis intervention, and understanding the complex factors that influence mental health and substance use. I possess strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills, along with the ability to approach sensitive conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism.

I understand that an effective Admissions Coordinator plays an essential role in connecting individuals and families with the appropriate level of care. I am particularly interested in applying my transferable skills to patient intake, initial screening and information gathering, referral coordination, insurance eligibility and benefits verification, admissions documentation, appointment scheduling, and follow-up communication. I recognize the importance of gathering accurate information, coordinating with clinical and administrative teams, maintaining confidentiality, and ensuring a smooth transition from initial inquiry to admission.

My strengths include active listening, compassionate family engagement, professional telephone communication, attention to detail, accurate data entry, organization, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a virtual environment. I also understand the importance of recognizing potentially urgent situations and promptly escalating clinical or safety concerns to the appropriate licensed professionals.

In addition to my academic background, I currently volunteer as a Research Assistant with the Canadian Pet Cancer Foundation, where I locate credible peer-reviewed research and prepare evidence-based summaries. This experience has strengthened my research, documentation, critical-thinking, and attention-to-detail skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my educational background, compassion, and dedication to behavioral health to your admissions team. Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because I know how much that first call can matter. In admissions at Clearday Treatment Center, I helped people who were reaching out for addiction treatment. Some were overwhelmed or unsure where to begin. I listened, answered their questions, and explained the next steps so they knew what to expect. That was the part of the work I found most meaningful, and it’s what drew me to this opportunity with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

At Wesley Family Services, I conducted phone intakes and helped older adults and their families connect with services. At Excela Neurology, I handled scheduling and cancellations in an office that received more than 100 calls a day, and I helped find room for urgent appointments. Those experiences taught me how to stay calm when calls are coming in quickly, keep track of details, and follow through when someone is waiting to hear back.

I’d welcome the opportunity to help the teens, adults, and families who reach out to your programs feel heard and know what to do next. Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,
Kristie Thomas

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,
I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role because I've spent my career being the person families reach on a hard day. As a foster care case manager and then as a district behavior specialist, my job was to take a family in crisis, figure out what they actually needed, and get them to a concrete next step. Being the first voice someone hears at Adolescent Wellness Academy or Principles Recovery Center is that same work, and it's the work I'm best at.
In foster care case management, I handled intake from the referral side: taking in cases, talking with parents and caregivers who were scared or angry, explaining an unfamiliar system in plain language, and coordinating with providers, schools, and agencies until a plan was in place. As a behavior specialist for the elementary schools in a Michigan district, I took referrals from staff and families, screened each one to decide what level of support fit, and walked parents through IEP and 504 processes so they understood their options. I'm calm on difficult calls, I don't rush people, and I keep the conversation pointed toward a clear next step.
I manage my own pipeline without daily direction. The behavior specialist role was new when I started, and I built it from nothing: referral forms, intake and ABC data tools, fidelity checklists, and the tracking systems that kept every open case moving across multiple buildings with no fixed schedule. Nothing fell through the cracks because I set up the follow-up structure myself and worked it every day. I'm comfortable learning new platforms quickly, and confidentiality is second nature after years of handling protected student and child-welfare records under FERPA and IDEA.
I'm especially drawn to this role. I know what it's like when a parent calls about a struggling kid and doesn't know where to start. I'm also a newly certified special education teacher, so I know how school, mental health, and family systems overlap for adolescents. For the population served by your organization, my foster care years gave me direct experience with families affected by substance use and co-occurring mental health needs, and I meet those callers without judgment. I hold current CPI and CPR/BLS certifications and have completed 40-hour RBT training.
I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can help callers get from that first conversation to admission. Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I’m interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position because it brings together the behavioral healthcare experience I’ve built over the years with the opportunity to help people navigate care at a time when they may feel overwhelmed or unsure where to turn.

My background includes more than 12 years in high-acuity behavioral healthcare, where I served in leadership roles overseeing health and wellness, coordinating care, and supporting patients, families, and multidisciplinary teams. Working in a demanding treatment environment taught me how important the first interaction can be. Families are often navigating difficult circumstances, and being able to listen without judgment, communicate clearly, and help them understand what comes next can make a meaningful difference.

In my role as Health and Wellness Director, I worked closely with physicians, psychiatrists, therapists, families, and staff to coordinate appropriate care. I was accustomed to managing competing priorities, responding to urgent situations, following up on outstanding needs, and maintaining accurate documentation. I also evaluated provider responsiveness and communication, addressed gaps in care processes, and developed staff training to improve consistency and accountability. These responsibilities required strong independent judgment and the ability to follow issues through rather than letting things fall through the cracks.

I also bring experience with electronic documentation through BestNotes, along with telehealth, and understand the importance of confidentiality and accurate recordkeeping in behavioral healthcare. Although my previous work was not a traditional admissions role, much of it involved helping people navigate a complicated healthcare situation, communicating with care providers, and making sure the next step in care was clear and appropriate.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, steady communication style, and genuine commitment to behavioral healthcare to your admissions team. I understand that the person answering the phone may be speaking with someone who has taken a great deal of courage to reach out, and I would take that responsibility seriously.

Thank you for your consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Lindsey Elliott

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a bilingual English-Spanish professional, virtual Spanish language instructor, and student pursuing an Associate of Applied Science in Human Services with a concentration in Addictions Counseling, I am passionate about supporting individuals and families navigating behavioral health challenges and accessing appropriate treatment.

My professional background includes experience in residential treatment environments, where I developed an appreciation for trauma-informed care, compassionate communication, and the importance of establishing trust with vulnerable populations. My academic studies continue to strengthen my understanding of substance use disorders, behavioral health, and individualized, person-centered approaches to care.

Additionally, through my work as a virtual Spanish language instructor, I independently coordinate online learning sessions, develop individualized educational materials, communicate with families, and facilitate engaging instruction in a remote environment. This experience has strengthened my organizational abilities, technological adaptability, time management, and capacity to establish meaningful professional relationships through virtual communication. My instructional philosophy emphasizes connection before correction, recognizing that effective communication begins with empathy, patience, and an understanding of individual needs.

I am also pursuing education in medical billing and coding, further expanding my understanding of healthcare administration, medical terminology, insurance processes, and accurate, confidential documentation. Together, these educational and professional experiences have equipped me with a multidisciplinary perspective that I believe would translate effectively into behavioral health admissions coordination.

On a personal level, navigating a complex healthcare journey as the parent of a medically complex child has strengthened my advocacy skills, resilience, and ability to communicate with multidisciplinary healthcare teams. This experience has deepened my understanding of the uncertainty families may experience when seeking specialized care and reinforced my commitment to ensuring individuals feel heard, respected, and supported throughout the process.

I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to serve as an initial point of contact for adolescents, adults, and families seeking behavioral health treatment. I recognize the importance of approaching these conversations with professionalism, cultural sensitivity, discretion, and compassion. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my bilingual communication skills, remote instructional experience, educational foundation, and commitment to behavioral healthcare to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to further discuss how my qualifications and dedication to service align with your organization’s mission.

Sincerely,
Allisson Harris

November 17, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Bachelor of Science in Human and Community Advocacy from the University of Texas at San Antonio, an Associate of Arts in Psychology, and professional experience in healthcare, customer service, and public assistance, I bring a combination of professional qualifications, compassion, and a genuine commitment to helping adolescents and families access mental health services.

Throughout my career, including my work with Texas Health and Human Services, healthcare-related call centers, and my current position with Aflac, I have developed strong skills in communication, active listening, documentation, problem-solving, and assisting individuals through complex and sometimes emotionally challenging situations. My experience has taught me the importance of maintaining confidentiality, gathering accurate information, explaining processes clearly, and ensuring that individuals feel respected and supported.

What makes this opportunity particularly meaningful to me is my personal experience as a mother who has navigated the mental health system while advocating for a child experiencing significant emotional and behavioral health challenges. I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my education, experience, and dedication to mental health advocacy would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Jermiane Rodriguez

Ashley Travillion-Shoulders
Monroe, Louisiana | 318-235-8688 | travillionashley@gmail.com

November 13, 2026

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a professional background in child welfare, family support, education, and customer service, I bring strong communication skills, compassion, and experience helping individuals and families navigate challenging situations.

Throughout my career, I have worked closely with children, parents, and families who needed guidance, reassurance, and access to appropriate resources. My experience in child welfare and family support strengthened my ability to handle sensitive conversations, assess individual needs, maintain confidential records, and coordinate services while remaining professional and empathetic. I understand the importance of making individuals feel heard, respected, and supported, particularly during difficult circumstances.

In my current role as an educator, I communicate regularly with families, address concerns, maintain accurate documentation, and collaborate with professionals to support students’ academic, behavioral, and emotional needs. My previous customer service experience with CenturyLink also strengthened my ability to manage inquiries, resolve concerns, and provide dependable follow-through.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of your organizations’ commitment to supporting adolescents, adults, and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I recognize how important that initial conversation can be and would approach each interaction with patience, professionalism, and genuine compassion. I am organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing multiple responsibilities while ensuring individuals receive timely information and clear next steps.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and people-centered approach to your admissions team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how my professional background could contribute to the meaningful work of your organizations.

Sincerely,
Ashley Travillion-Shoulders

Hiring Committee

Re: Program Director, Virtual Intensive Outpatient Program

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to apply for the Program Director, Virtual IOP position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With over a decade of progressive leadership experience at Hazelden Betty Ford and Caron Treatment Centers, I have built, expanded, and led behavioral health programs that combine clinical excellence with sustainable business performance. What particularly attracts me to this opportunity is the chance to bring together two areas where I have demonstrated significant success: developing accessible virtual treatment services and leading programs through strategic growth.

At Hazelden Betty Ford, I spearheaded the development and implementation of English and Spanish virtual behavioral health services in just two weeks during the COVID-19 pandemic. This required rapidly establishing clinical workflows, adapting treatment delivery to a virtual environment, supporting multidisciplinary teams, and maintaining continuity of care without compromising clinical quality. Beyond this initiative, I helped standardize intensive outpatient programming and curriculum across multiple markets, including Minnesota, New York, Chicago, and California. These experiences strengthened my ability to scale accessible treatment models while maintaining operational consistency and clinical integrity.

Currently, as Senior Clinical Director for Caron Treatment Centers in Florida, I provide strategic and operational leadership across a comprehensive continuum of behavioral healthcare services. My responsibilities encompass clinical operations, financial performance, program development, staff leadership, regulatory compliance, and quality improvement. I have helped expand treatment capacity from startup operations to approximately 75 beds within months, supported programs serving more than 500 patients annually, and implemented systems to strengthen documentation quality, operational accountability, and the patient experience.

What distinguishes my leadership approach is the belief that exceptional clinical care and strong business performance are mutually reinforcing. Sustainable census growth depends on meaningful referral relationships, reliable operational systems, measurable outcomes, and an experience that earns the trust of patients, families, and community partners. I lead with a commitment to high standards, thoughtful innovation, and personalized service, ensuring that operational decisions ultimately strengthen the quality and accessibility of care.

Adolescent Wellness Academy’s family-centered approach and commitment to expanding access to treatment for adolescents strongly resonate with me. I would welcome the opportunity to apply my experience in virtual care development, multidisciplinary leadership, financial oversight, and program growth to build a high-performing Virtual IOP that creates meaningful outcomes for young people and their families throughout Florida.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and leadership philosophy can contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s continued growth and mission.

Sincerely,

Manuel Garcia, MA, LADC, CAC, ICADC

To whom it may concern,
My name is Selena, and I am excited to be applying for the primary therapist position at North Carolina's first-ever AWA location! I am an LCSWA with multiple years of experience providing therapeutic support in numerous capacities, including as a behavioral health technician, case manager, and psychotherapist. I've also gained experience in a diverse range of therapeutic settings, such as an inpatient adolescent hospital, PHP/IOP mental health clinics, community health (including in-home), and outpatient therapy. The most influential experiences I've gained have been working in adolescent inpatient and PHP/IOP clinics, in which I became comfortable leading group therapy sessions, providing 1:1 individual therapy as well as family-based therapy, and working collaboratively with clinical teams consisting of numerous disciplines and treatment goals. I've also become comfortable with higher levels of care, which I am able to use to offer clients validation and unconditional positive regard, as these experiences can be exhausting. In my current outpatient work, I primarily work with pre-teens and adolescents, as I witnessed a gap in care for these age groups despite the intensity of these transformative years. I aspire to be a supportive resource to these clients in whatever capacity I am able to, as it is already difficult to be a teen, let alone one who feels misunderstood and alone in the journey.

Abigail Cornele
910-330-5752
acornele42@gmail.com

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy (AWA)
Mooresville, NC

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy
Mooresville, North Carolina

Re: Operations Manager, Behavioral Health

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Operations Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. What particularly attracted me to this opportunity is the chance to be part of a founding team and help establish a supportive, well-organized environment for adolescents and their families. With a Master’s degree in Counselling Psychology, two years of full-time experience working directly with mental health clients, and a background in operations management, staff supervision, and business administration, I believe I can bring a valuable combination of clinical understanding and operational leadership to your new North Carolina location.

As the founder of HAP TherapyCare, I independently established and managed a virtual psychotherapy practice while providing direct mental health services. Beyond working with clients, I was responsible for nearly every aspect of running the practice, including client inquiries, intake, scheduling, billing, clinical documentation, professional referrals, and maintaining appropriate standards of confidentiality and care. This experience gave me an appreciation for how much the quality of a client’s experience depends on what happens behind the scenes. Clear communication, reliable processes, timely follow-up, and a welcoming environment can make a meaningful difference for individuals and families seeking support.

My operational leadership experience extends beyond healthcare. At Toronto Inspection Ltd., I coordinated 10 to 15 field technicians and more than 20 daily site visits across multiple active projects while guiding administrative staff, resolving escalations, and improving documentation processes. I regularly investigated complex operational and billing discrepancies, worked with different stakeholders to identify solutions, and introduced practical improvements to make daily operations more organized and efficient. I also bring experience in employee recruitment, interviewing, onboarding, training, and supervision, along with additional business administration and payroll responsibilities through my work with Saphgen.

One quality I would particularly bring to Adolescent Wellness Academy is a strong sense of ownership. When something is not working, I naturally want to understand why, explore possible solutions, and follow through until the issue is addressed. I enjoy creating structure, supporting colleagues, and finding ways to make people’s work easier without losing sight of the individuals we serve. My counselling background has also shaped how I lead and communicate, with empathy, patience, accountability, and respect for different perspectives.

I understand that launching a new behavioral health clinic requires flexibility, collaboration, and attention to both operational details and the experiences of clients, families, and staff. Although I have not previously managed an adolescent PHP or IOP program, I am eager to build on my existing experience, learn the specific requirements of your programs, and contribute to establishing strong operational foundations from the beginning.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in mental health services, practice management, and operational leadership could support Adolescent Wellness Academy’s expansion into North Carolina. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Sincerely,
Hareesma Amutha Venkatesan

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in Studio Art and Psychology, as well as experience in Special Education and Applied Behavior Analysis, I have always been drawn to the ways creativity can help us connect, express ourselves, and discover more about who we are. I would love the opportunity to bring this perspective into a setting that supports adolescents through their mental health journeys.

In my current role as a SpEd Art Teacher, I work with students with diverse learning needs, developing creative activities to encourage their exploration and independence. My approach to art is centered on the process rather than the final product; I believe the arts should be an opportunity to experiment, take risks, make mistakes, and express yourself without the pressure of getting something "right." My previous experience as an ABA Teacher has also taught me the importance of meeting individuals where they are and creating supportive environments where everyone feels welcome to participate.

My creative background extends beyond visual art to include writing, music, and theatre. These experiences have deepened my appreciation for the many ways people communicate and express themselves, and I'm drawn to opportunities that allow others to explore those possibilities.

This is an environment I hope to foster for others; one where individuals feel safe to explore their emotions, connect with each other, and perhaps even learn something new about themselves along the way.

I was drawn to this opportunity because of AWA's commitment to creating a supportive, welcoming, and structured environment for adolescents and their families.

Through my internship at My Optimal Child, I gained experience in a behavioral health setting, where I assisted with administrative and organizational responsibilities, prepared materials, organized documents, and had the opportunity to observe therapists working with children, teens, and families. This experience helped me develop a greater understanding of the importance of maintaining an organized and supportive environment in a behavioral health practice.

Additionally, I have several years of babysitting experience, which has strengthened my ability to demonstrate patience, take responsibility, and create a safe and positive environment for children. I consider myself dependable, and willing to take initiative wherever help is needed.
I would be excited to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy by helping maintain a clean, organized, and welcoming facility while supporting the daily operations of the program. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further and look forward to hearing from you.

Sincerely,

 Anna Babinchak
